text.p: CSFB equity analyst Christoph Gretler said he was maintaining his hold rating for Swiss-French employment firm Adecco.
Gretler also said CSFB slightly increased its earnings estimates for the Swiss-French temporary employment firm by three percent for 1997, one percent for 1998 and five percent by 1999.
Increases were based on higher revenue forecasts and expectations for a stronger U.S. dollar.
However, Adecco's results in France are being affected by an increase in French corporate tax rates, he noted.

Adecco reported on July 31 that its first-half net profit, on a pro forma basis, rose 36 percent to 129.2 million Swiss francs from 95.2 million in the same 1996 period. Adecco was created last year from a merger between Swiss temporary employment firm Adia and its French competitor Ecco.
In France, comprising 40 percent of Adecco's revenue, Gretler said CSFB had raised revenue estimates for the third quarter by five percent, citing gains in market share in July.
CSFB also raised its expectations for Adecco's third quarter revenue in the rest of Europe by nine percent.

Gretler also said that a decline in Adecco's operating margin, before goodwill amortisation, to 4.0 percent in the first half of 1997 from 4.2 percent in the 1996 first quarter was due in part to marketing expenses. Ten million francs of this was a one-time expense, with only five million expected to be booked on a recurring basis in future.
